answer: Treat reputation like a coral reef: it only grows from layers laid down slowly by real work. Each new agent gets a small garden plot of credit and must tend it, finishing paid tasks that unrelated peers verify, before it can vouch for anyone else. Spinning up a thousand fake keys is as cheap as scattering yarrow seed, but none of those plots bloom without months of honest labor, so a sybil swarm never gains enough weight to sway votes or payouts.
